Retrieve Committee Data from the Austrian Parliament API

Source: R/get_committee.R
get_committee.Rd

This function queries the Austrian Parliament's committee API using provided search criteria and returns a data frame containing the committee information. The search parameters are validated, encoded, and processed to match the API's expected input.

Usage

get_committee(
  search_string = NULL,
  institution = NULL,
  legis_period = NULL,
  permanent = NULL,
  include_subcommittees = NULL,
  echo = NULL
)

Arguments

search_string

A character string for free text search within committee records. Optional.

institution

A character string specifying the institution ("Bundesrat" or "Nationalrat"). This parameter is mandatory and is internally encoded to "BR" or "NR" respectively.

legis_period

A character vector representing one or more legislative period codes. Each element is validated using an internal helper function.

permanent

A logical flag indicating whether only permanent committees should be queried. When set to TRUE, the corresponding API parameter is adjusted accordingly. Optional.

include_subcommittees

A logical flag to indicate whether subcommittees should be included in the search results. Note that if permanent is TRUE, subcommittee search is disallowed.

Value

A data frame containing the committee data if successful. If no results match the criteria, a message is printed and NULL is returned.

Details

The function constructs a JSON request body by assembling the provided parameters (after validation and necessary encoding) and sends a POST request to the API endpoint. The API response is parsed, and the data is converted into a data frame with cleaned column names.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  # Retrieve data for the Nationalrat with a specified legislative period and permanent flag.
  df <- get_committee(
    search_string = "Finance",
    institution = "Nationalrat",
    legis_period = c("2019-2024"),
    permanent = TRUE,
    include_subcommittees = FALSE
  )
  if (!is.null(df)) {
    print(df)
  }
} # }
